alignments.note: Waw rendered *Or* (rule 14); the list of connectives is read off the ASV.

The אִם opening this disjunctive question has no English of its own: the ASV marks the question by inversion alone, fronting the possessive verb rather than writing a separate auxiliary (rule 17). Rules 20 and 50 give the particle a fronted finite word only where it is the construction's own copula or an existential frame; the possessive *hast* is rule 43's and belongs to the morpheme that makes the clause possessive.

The possessive לְ heading this verbless clause is what makes it possessive and carries the English *have* (rule 43); dropping *hast* leaves only the possession relation unstated, which is that rule's subtraction test.
Suffix of the possessive לְ takes the English subject pronoun (rule 43).
Indefinite article belongs to the noun that licenses it (rule 15).
Assimilated article token with no *the* written for it (rules 12, 29).
Verb with its modal and subject pronoun; no interrogative morpheme stands in this second clause, so the fronted *canst* is the verb's own (rule 17). Head on the lexical verb.
Indefinite article belongs to the noun (rule 15).

review_notes: *hast* is the possessive לְ's under rule 43 and אִם is `unrepresented` under rule 17's inversion-only sentence. The competing reading, which the first pass took, gives *hast* to the particle under rules 20 and 50; it is rejected because those rules reach a construction-supplied copula and an existential frame, while a possessive *have* is a recasting rule 43 assigns to the morpheme that makes the clause possessive — and giving it to the particle left the לְ holding nothing while its own relation carried the clause.

The second clause writes no interrogative morpheme, so its fronted *canst* stays with תַרְעֵם under rule 17's last-sentence limit; the two halves of the verse differ because a particle stands in the first and not in the second.
The assimilated article [הַ] is `unrepresented`: the ASV renders `אֵל` anarthrously as the name *God* (rules 12, 29).
